# Concepts

> v6.6 documentation section. Applicability within this branch is unknown unless a linked page says otherwise.

- [Apps](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/v6.6/concepts/extensions/apps-concept.md): Apps: The app system allows you to extend and modify the functionality and appearance of Shopware. It leverages well defined extension points you can hook into to implement your specific use case.
- [Architecture](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/v6.6/concepts/framework/architecture.md): Architecture: On a high level, Shopware consists of multiple modules that separate the entire code base into logical units. Some modules are independent, and some depend on others.
- [Cart](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/v6.6/concepts/commerce/checkout-concept/cart.md): Cart: Shopping cart management is a central feature of Shopware 6. The shopping cart resides in the checkout bundle and is a central part of the checkout process.
- [Catalog](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/v6.6/concepts/commerce/catalog.md): Catalog: In this section, we will go through the structure that organizes products, prices and everything related to maintaining a product catalog within the store.
- [Categories](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/v6.6/concepts/commerce/catalog/categories.md): Categories: Products in Shopware are organized in categories. - [Content](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/v6.6/concepts/commerce/content.md): Content: Shopware 6 has an integrated content management system based upon layouts which is called Shopping Experiences. The tool used to compose and manage layouts is part of the Admin panel and referred to as Page Builder.
- [Data Abstraction Layer](https://developer.shopware.com/docs/v6.6/concepts/framework/data-abstraction-layer.md): Data Abstraction Layer: In contrast to most Symfony applications, Shopware uses no ORM, but a thin abstraction layer called the data abstraction layer \(DAL\).
